context.body: Royal splendor becomes a contrast for unearned divine care in creation.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Jesus directs disciples from anxiety to ravens and lilies, saying Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one flower.
observations.label: Luke remembers Solomon’s glory among the lilies: action

observations.body: Hearers are called to seek God’s Kingdom rather than live by anxious pursuit.
observations.label: Luke remembers Solomon’s glory among the lilies: response

observations.body: ravens · lilies · Solomon in all his glory · seek God’s Kingdom
observations.label: Words in Luke 12:22–31

payload.posture: Read Luke 12:22–31 as later memory and aftermath evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The saying relativizes Solomon’s glory without denying the reality of human need.
payload.title: Luke remembers Solomon’s glory among the lilies
